subject: Proposal: 3-year prepay & rate guarantee to avoid renewal step-up
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@fastretail.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@fastretail.com, kevin.tan@fastretail.com
Date: 2027-03-13T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal options — concerns about rate increases

Hi Ben,

We received the renewal notice for our Redwood account and are reviewing budget for FY28. Leadership is concerned about the projected per-token rate increases we saw in the renewal summary. Before we put a recommendation together, can you share if Redwood offers any multi-year prepay options to lock current pricing?

Two asks from our side:
- A simple pricing example that shows the effective rate (tokens/month) and any ramp schedule required.
- Any contractual language or guarantees you can offer to prevent step-ups during the term.

If possible, include options for both an annual prepay and a 3-year prepay with staged usage. We need this by next Friday for our procurement review.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Head of Platform Products
FastRetail
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Julia Park <julia.park@fastretail.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-14T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal options — concerns about rate increases

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the note and the clear asks. Short answer: yes — we offer a multi-year prepay that can lock your unit economics and include a rate guarantee clause. I attached a 3-year term sheet and a simple ramp workbook so your finance team can model the cashflow. Key highlights up front:

- 3-year prepay example: 60% prepay Year 1, 25% Year 2, 15% Year 3.
- Effective discount: 18% off list token rate if you commit to the suggested ramp.
- Rate guarantee: fixed per-token rate for the contract term (contract includes a renegotiation carve-out for material changes to infrastructure costs).
- Flexibility: ability to draw down prepay early (we credit unused months toward later months) and a limited overage pool at a slightly higher tier.

Attached: redwood_3yr-prepay-term-sheet.pdf and fastretail-map_ramp.xlsx.

If it helps, I can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with Monica from Customer Success to go through the ramp sheet and the operational guarantees (cache behavior, burst lanes, SLA).

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: procurement@fastretail.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: julia.park@fastretail.com, kevin.tan@fastretail.com
Date: 2027-03-15T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal options — concerns about rate increases

Ben, Julia —

Appreciate the materials. Two clarifying questions from procurement/finance:

1) Can you confirm how refunds/credits for unused prepay are handled if actual usage falls below the committed draw (we prefer quarterly true-ups rather than long lock-ins).
2) The ramp worksheet includes a Year 1 heavy-front load (60%). Can you provide an alternative schedule that evens the burn (e.g., 40/35/25) and show the delta in discount?

We also need a procurement-level summary (one pager) with contract language for the rate guarantee and any termination/exit provisions for our legal review.

Thanks —
Procurement Team
FastRetail
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: procurement@fastretail.com, julia.park@fastretail.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-16T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal options — concerns about rate increases

Hi Procurement —

Answers below and attached a short procurement summary.

1) Unused prepay handling:
- Quarterly true-up: we calculate usage vs. committed draw at each quarter. If actual usage < committed draw, customer receives a credit applied to the following quarter. For multi-year terms we can also offer an annual reconciliation and an option to reallocate credits between years (subject to business review).

2) Alternate ramp: attached sheet "fastretail-map_ramp_alt" shows 40% / 35% / 25% with a resulting effective discount of 15% (vs 18% on the front-loaded profile).

Procurement one-pager: included as page 1 of redwood_3yr-prepay-term-sheet.pdf — it explicitly calls out the rate guarantee clause (Section 2.1) and an early-termination pro-rated credit calculation (Section 7).

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm which ramp profile you prefer (60/25/15 vs 40/35/25) by EOD Tuesday.
- I will then prepare a DocuSign envelope with the term summary for signature and route the final contract to your legal contact.

Monica — could you join a 20-min call Tuesday to walk the team through the operational controls?

Thanks,
Ben

We ran the alternate ramp in our finance model and prefer the 40/35/25 split (smoother capex profile). The 15% effective discount is acceptable provided the rate guarantee language is signed into the contract and the quarterly true-up mechanism is documented.

Please send the DocuSign link and the procurement one-pager to kevin.tan@fastretail.com and legal@fastretail.com. Once we have the DocuSign envelope we will route internally and aim to return a signature within 3 business days.
